chemprop2019.citation: Yang et al., J. Chem. Inf. Model. 59, 3370-3389 (2019) - D-MPNN / chemprop, arXiv:1904.01561v5
chemprop2019.note: Table 4 gives the dataset sizes (ESOL 1128, FreeSolv 642, Lipophilicity 4200, BACE 1513 - identical to the CSVs used here). The per-dataset result panels are figures, not numeric tables, so no D-MPNN scalar can be transcribed from the text; this source is therefore only used to attest the molecule counts and the split protocol (10 randomly-seeded 80:10:10 splits, scaffold split for headline results, random-split results moved to the Supporting Information).

grover2020.citation: Rong et al., NeurIPS 33 (2020) - GROVER, arXiv:2007.02835v2
grover2020.note: Table 1 (p. 7): classification ROC-AUC and regression RMSE with standard deviations. Sec. 4.2 and Appendix B.1 state: 'we apply the scaffold splitting for all tasks on all datasets' and 'three independent runs on three random-seeded scaffold splitting'. Split seeds are not published, so the exact indices cannot be reproduced or matched.

molnet2018.citation: Wu et al., Chem. Sci. 9, 513-530 (2018) - MoleculeNet
molnet2018.note: Table 1 (dataset table: split method per dataset) and Table 3 (best performance per dataset, conventional vs graph-based). No per-example split indices are published; the paper reports one number per model, not a multi-seed mean.

transcription: values copied by hand from the fetched documents; locators give the table and row. GROVER's regression panel is a scaffold-split panel, which is why its ESOL/FreeSolv/Lipophilicity numbers are graded C against a random-split round.
why: No published source releases the per-example split indices behind its numbers, and the published random/scaffold draws are seed-dependent, so A-grade (EXACT_SPLIT_MATCH) is unreachable for these four datasets. Within-grade B comparisons are still valid for the protocol-matched rows.
